quarterly_data.signal: Total revenue record $22.2 billion, up 48% year-on-year; semiconductor revenue record $15 billion up 79% year-on-year; AI semiconductor revenue record $10.8 billion up 143% year-on-year
Q2 bookings for AI semiconductors were over $30 billion against $10.8 billion shipped; bookings exceed 3x quarterly shipments
Full year 2026 AI semiconductor revenue expected to be $56 billion, up approximately 180% from fiscal 2025
AI semiconductor revenue guidance for fiscal 2027 to be in excess of $100 billion; expect growth to continue in fiscal 2028
Q2 operating income record $14.9 billion up 52% year-on-year; operating margin record 67%; adjusted EBITDA $15.2 billion or 69% of revenue
Free cash flow record $10.3 billion, 46% of revenue; capex $231 million; cash $19.6 billion; inventory $4.3 billion at 86 days on hand

Q3 2026 guidance: consolidated revenue $29.4 billion up 84% year-on-year; semiconductor revenue $20.5 billion up 124%; AI semiconductor revenue $16 billion up over 200%; software revenue $8.9 billion up 31%
Planning to ship 10 gigawatts of XPU compute capacity in 2027; back-half loaded
AI XPU platform being created with Apollo, Blackstone, and other investors to deploy more than 20 gigawatts of compute capacity; first tranche valued at $35 billion currently being launched by Apollo
Purchase orders totaling $6 billion received to date from two newer customers (other than Google, Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI)
Non-AI semiconductor revenue Q2 $4.2 billion up 6% year-on-year; Q3 forecast $4.5 billion up 12%
Infrastructure software Q2 revenue $7.2 billion up 9% year-on-year; ARR growth 17% year-over-year; Q3 forecast $8.9 billion up 31%
Gross margin 77.1% in Q2, expected to decline to ~74% in Q3 due to mix shift toward AI semiconductors; semiconductor segment gross margin approximately 70%; software gross margin 93%
Inventory days on hand increased to 86 days in Q2 from 68 days in Q1 in anticipation of accelerating AI semiconductor growth in second half
Order visibility now extends all the way to 2028; 3 months ago visibility ran through 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Multiple 800G Ethernet switch programs ramping across the largest hyperscaler customers (plus continued 400G); 1.6T switch programs beginning mass production in 2H 2026 with two hyperscaler customers — 10 active 1.6T programs ramping heavily into 2027. Landmark win: a 1.6T co-packaged-optics (CPO) Ethernet switch for a hyperscaler — believed to be the first major production-scale CPO deployment, integrating a Broadcom Tomahawk module directly into the system (mass production 2H 2027). Also a 'digital native' fully-integrated compute+networking rack-scale program entering production in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: 800G ramping; 10 active 1.6T programs; 1.6T CPO (Broadcom Tomahawk) win, MP 2H2027

quarterly_data.signal: Switch production cadence: multiple 800G Ethernet switch programs ramping now; MASS PRODUCTION of 1.6T switch programs begins with TWO hyperscaler customers in H2 2026; the landmark 1.6T co-packaged-optics Ethernet switch win reaches mass production in 2027. Management's CPO view: each hyperscaler adopts on its own path — some choose CPX before CPO — and 'the major adoption will be at 3.2T'. Supply, not demand, is pacing growth (extended lead times on advanced components; demand 'durable and cumulative').
